body.statement: If every \(p_z\), every coordinate of \(v_z\), and every \(q_\theta\) is rational, then the observable-margin primal and dual programs admit rational optimizers. Finite rational feasibility, equality of the two rational objectives, and complementary slackness form an exact primal--dual certificate; the same implementation formula yields rational assignment-level tables.
body.justification: Rationality is needed for machine-checkable exact certificates, not for the observable-function or Pareto characterization.
body.gap: The exact finite certificate is a computational corollary of the all-observable program, whereas \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} certifies a matrix-quadratic program.
body.consumer: Auditors can verify a reported finite optimum using rational arithmetic with no numerical tolerance.
